This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 42 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 52ffd5aad531d8c891a5b47aee80fe38c093eeec` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bc3c33693589dba6582880d161fabac303fb14cc` — the merge of head `5553a6fd37a166b1baec6201d43c259c060b4f94` into base `52ffd5aad531d8c891a5b47aee80fe38c093eeec`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bc3c33693589dba6582880d161fabac303fb14cc && git checkout bc3c33693589dba6582880d161fabac303fb14cc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 52ffd5aad531d8c891a5b47aee80fe38c093eeec 5553a6fd37a166b1baec6201d43c259c060b4f94 && git checkout -B drift-repro 52ffd5aad531d8c891a5b47aee80fe38c093eeec && git merge --no-ff 5553a6fd37a166b1baec6201d43c259c060b4f94

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 52ffd5aad531d8c891a5b47aee80fe38c093eeec
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 52ffd5aad531d8c891a5b47aee80fe38c093eeec` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `48519a26568969d0bbed8a2fae7de4757ee3347f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + packages/spec/liveness/field.json

Inputs: card #31910 (body, triage 6739506120, unblock 6741976364, claim 6742064425, claim amend 1 6742143275, os-dev-report 6743591282), PR #31956 (body, file list, net diff against merge base `cc6e2824`), the check-runs on the head (every run `success` or `skipped`, none failed), ruling A record 6739066323 on #31743, and the merged ADR-0144 text on `origin/main` (the two Amended notes under D2 and D6, the Consequences note, Open item 14). The rest of the diff (the test harness, the three regenerated `content/docs/references/**` pages, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the changeset is read here only for ②. Code outside the diff was read, never reviewed: `refuseDishonestRecordCurrencyField`, `refuseDishonestHomeAmount`, `FieldNameKeySchema` and `ObjectExtensionSchema` in object.zod.ts; `collectLookupAutofillErrors` and `defineStack`'s parse-then-cross-reference order in stack.zod.ts; `metadata-type-schemas.ts` (`field: FieldSchema` registered standalone); objectql `record-currency-code.ts#recordCurrencyFieldOf`, `record-currency-aggregate-door.ts#recordCurrencySummaryRefusal` and `engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts`'s relationship-field scan; `packages/spec/scripts/liveness/undrilled-containers.baseline.json`; `lint-liveness-properties.ts`; AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3; SKILL.md's `Skills-docs:` grammar; card #31957.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Two-segment `currencyField` admitted on `ObjectSchema` — right.** field.zod.ts:557 admits `PARENT_FIELD.CODE_FIELD` (exactly two snake_case segments) under `record`; object.zod.ts:1962 and :2025 admit it only when segment 1 is a declared `master_detail` of the same object. This is ruling A's first sentence and the amended D2 note word for word: one hop, `master_detail` only. A `formula` with `returnType: 'currency'` carries the same config and so follows the same way; the ADR's TL;DR says "an amount on a `master_detail` child", and a formula is an amount, so this is inside the ruling, not wider.
2. **`lookup` refused with its own sentence — right.** object.zod.ts:2068. The D2 note: "The ruling names `master_detail` only, so a path through a `lookup` stays refused."
3. **Three or more segments, an empty or non-snake_case segment refused — right in substance** (one hop; the D2 note says "the two-segment form"), **but see ① 7 for where it is judged.**
4. **The `summary` spells its currency as a one-segment `record` pointer at the parent's own code field, no new key — right.** field.zod.ts:753 and :2285 describe it; the shape already parsed on `main` (`refuseDishonestRecordCurrencyField` judged the one-segment pointer on every `record` config, summary included). The D6 note left the spelling to this card; a reader that resolves a record-mode amount off its row resolves the roll-up off the parent row with nothing added. **A path on a `summary` refused** (object.zod.ts:2038) — right, and not a narrowing: on `main` every dotted pointer was refused inside an object (① 7 explains why).
5. **Stack door (a) — right.** stack.zod.ts:4539 judges segment 2 on the object the `master_detail` references as a `VALUE_DOMAIN_FIELD_TYPES` field with `valueDomain: 'iso_4217_currency'`, the D2 note's "a code field of the kind the first bullet requires". Segment 1 not a `master_detail` or the parent not in the stack ⇒ skipped, the `collectLookupAutofillErrors` stance claim amend 1 ordered. The one-config door and the object door cannot see the parent, so stack level is the right place, and the registry at runtime registration (#31911) is named as the other reader.
6. **Stack door (b) — right in what it judges, right in what it leaves alone.** stack.zod.ts:4560-4595: only a `sum`/`min`/`max`/`avg` summary over a child amount that follows a path, through the very `master_detail` that path starts with (`amountVia.reference === objectName` and `relation === amount.via`), is required to declare `currencyConfig: { currencyMode: 'record', currencyField: CODE_FIELD }` naming the followed code field. `count` is skipped (`summaryFunctionReadsField`); a child with its own code field, or a roll-up through another relation, is left to D6's first bullet, which `recordCurrencySummaryRefusal` enforces at registration. That is the D6 note's "admitted only through that very `master_detail` field" with nothing wider. A path whose code the parent lacks is told once at the amount (:4579), not again at the roll-up.
7. **Accept-set narrowing on three public parse surfaces — wrong as declared (should-fix 1).** The spelling door is attached to `CurrencyConfigSchema` (field.zod.ts:632), so it also runs on `FieldSchema` parsed standalone (the registered `field` metadata type, `metadata-type-schemas.ts`, reached by `PUT /api/v1/meta/field/:name` and the Studio field form), on `CurrencyConfigSchema` itself (exported), and on `ObjectExtensionSchema.fields` (object.zod.ts:5254 on `main`, whose `superRefine` applies no record-currency door by precedent). On `main` each of those accepted `{ currencyMode: 'record', currencyField: 'a.b.c' }` and `'Sales_Order.currency_code'`; on this head each refuses them. Inside `ObjectSchema` the change IS a pure widening: `FieldNameKeySchema` (object.zod.ts:2960 on `main`) admits no dot in a field key, so `refuseDishonestRecordCurrencyField`'s `hasOwnProperty(map, target)` was false for every dotted pointer and refused it. The dev measured on `ObjectSchema` alone ("nothing that parsed before is refused"). The narrowed inputs never resolved anywhere (the engine reads the pointer as a sibling name, and no row key can be dotted, so every write of an amount beside one was refused `ERR_CURRENCY_CODE_REQUIRED`), which is why this is a should-fix and not a FAIL, but it is a declaration the gates read, not a nit.
8. **`homeAmount.rateField` sharing by spelling — right.** object.zod.ts:2271-2293 (code unchanged; comment new). Two amounts store one rate exactly when they convert from one code on one date. Two paths spelled alike name one `master_detail`, hence one parent row and one code field; a path and a one-segment sibling are two values; two paths through two `master_detail` fields are two parent rows. Pointer equality by spelling is the exact predicate, and both negative cases are pinned.
9. **No public export added or changed — right.** `summaryFunctionReadsField` and `VALUE_DOMAIN_FIELD_TYPES` were already exported from field.zod.ts; stack.zod.ts:44 only imports them. `api-surface/` and `authorable-surface/` unchanged; `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check:generated`) is green on the head.
10. **A lookup path on an extension field is judged nowhere in spec — right by precedent, owed to #31911.** `ObjectExtensionSchema` skips the object door (as it skips the one-segment dishonest-pointer door today), and (a) skips a non-`master_detail` segment 1. The registry at registration owes it; the PR body's acceptance note 2 says so.
11. **A parent known only through an `objectExtension` is refused, wrongly (should-fix 2).** See ④.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/31910-record-currency-follows-parent.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. **Level right either way** (AGENTS.md step 3: any kind other than `none` takes at least `minor`). **Kind and arm depend on how should-fix 1 is resolved.** As the tree stands, a record-mode value that parsed on three public surfaces is refused, and step 3 reads "a value refused or a requirement tightened is `narrowed`; several ⇒ `narrowed` over `semantic` over `added`", and the `Clause-②` grammar's spelling for "widens one surface and narrows another" is `yes (narrowing)` (clause2-line.mjs). If the dev takes remedy (ii) below the declarations are right as written.
- The changeset's "Still refused" sentence is accurate; the "pure widening" claim lives in the PR body (风险与回滚), not in the changeset. `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are green on the head.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` with `minor` is the right pairing for the admitted shapes (#31424 rule 2, triage 6739506120).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation 1** (stack-door pins in the existing `currency-config-record-mode.test.ts` harness, not a file beside stack.zod.ts): the lane seat's; the harness already imports `defineStack` the way `field-lookup-autofill.test.ts` does. Accepted. Ablation counts (7 / 2 / 1 / 5) are the dev's account and not relied on here; the pins themselves were read and cover each door and both rate-sharing negatives.
- **Dev deviation 2** ((b) judges only roll-ups over a path-following child): right, and the reason it is no narrowing at stack level. Accepted.
- **Dev deviation 3 (liveness):** `field/currencyConfig` and `field/summaryOperations` are both in the `containers` list of `packages/spec/scripts/liveness/undrilled-containers.baseline.json` (verified; the PR body's path `scripts/liveness/…` is a misspelling, nit N4). With one blanket row each and no key added, there is no coordinate to grade `planned`, so each row keeps `live` and its `note` gains a dated WIDENED entry naming the two new shapes as PLANNED with #31911 (objectql) and #31912 (Console) as readers (field.json:131, :439). Accepted as the only honest shape short of drilling the container, which is evidence work outside this card. Consequence named: `lint-liveness-properties.ts` reads `status`, never `note`, so the `liveness-planned-property` author warning cannot fire for these shapes while the blanket row is `live`. `Spec property liveness` is green on the head.
- **open_questions (release pairing):** the seat ruled A. Judged on this tree: the describe text (field.zod.ts:795, :805, :2285) states the contract and says nothing about the engine, which is where the repo keeps describe text; not-yet-read state lives in the ledger, which carries it. Until #31911, a write of a following child amount is refused `ERR_CURRENCY_CODE_REQUIRED` (`record-currency-code.ts`: `recordCurrencyFieldOf` returns the path as a sibling name, the image has no such key, the refusal fires) and such a roll-up is refused at registration by `recordCurrencySummaryRefusal`; nothing is stored wrong. Both are loud, so A is tenable. One input for the seat's call, not a finding on this tree: that refusal's message prescribes writing the code into `'sales_order.currency_code'` on the child, a field the child does not have, so an author who follows the describe meets a loud but misdirecting prescription until #31911 lands.
- **`Skills-docs: follow-up owed #31957`:** #31957 exists, `domain:skills`, `Blocked-by: #31910, #31911`, and teaches the three things this diff admits (path through `master_detail` only, the summary spelling, the lock). Right in substance; spelling is nit N3.
- **Metadata-protocol: added:** see ② and should-fix 1.
- **out_of_scope_findings:** the class-c inert `currencyConfig` on summaries over other children, the Studio `field.form.ts` help text, and the skills follow-up are the seat's; none is a defect in this diff.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay-author note owed. The PR is a draft; a record on a draft's head is in order.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts** — against the amended D2 note and its first consumers (the object door, and `FieldSchema` parsed standalone by the metadata API and Studio).
- The door (:557) judges spelling alone and leaves what the segments name to the object and the stack; the chain at :626-:640 keeps every non-`record` branch byte-identical. The three describe texts (:795, :805, :2285) match the code: two segments, `master_detail` only, "never a `lookup`", the summary's one-segment spelling. Holds.
- **Should-fix 1 — field.zod.ts:632 (door :557), .changeset line 7-8, PR body.** The declaration and the tree disagree (① 7). Two remedies, the dev's choice: (i) keep the door where it is and declare what it does — `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on body and changeset, with the one-line disposition that the refused pointers never named a field (no field key holds a dot) and no stored row can have written an amount beside one, so a stored metadata row carrying one fails its next parse loudly and had never worked; or (ii) keep the accept set exactly by judging the spelling only where a dotted pointer was already refused, the object door (object.zod.ts:2034-2035 already re-splits and returns on a malformed one; make it refuse there instead), leaving `CurrencyConfigSchema`, standalone `FieldSchema` and `ObjectExtensionSchema` accepting what they accepted on `main` — the stack door's `recordCurrencyPathOf` (:4462) already skips a malformed pointer. (ii) loses a spelling refusal the Studio field form never had; (i) carries a BREAKING arm for inputs that were dead on write. Either makes the declaration true; the record does not pick for the seat.

**packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts** — against ruling A and the D2 note, and its first consumer (`defineStack`'s object parse, then the stack door).
- :1962 routes a dotted pointer to the path door before the one-segment refusals, so the one-segment messages never fire on a path. The path door (:2025) refuses in the right order: malformed spelling is the config door's and is not told twice; a `summary` is refused with the one-segment prescription; segment 1 undeclared, then non-`master_detail` with the lookup-specific sentence. Every refusal names the `master_detail` candidates. Self-referencing `master_detail` is left to the stack door, which resolves the same map. Holds; pure widening inside `ObjectSchema` (① 7).
- :2271-:2293 rate sharing: see ① 8. Holds.

**packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts** — against the D2 and D6 notes, claim amend 1, and the `collectLookupAutofillErrors` precedent (:4410).
- :5361 runs after `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse`, so segment 1 has passed the object door by the time (a) runs, as the JSDoc says. Unresolved parent skipped (:4539, pinned). (a)'s two refusals carry the parent's code-field candidates. (b)'s skip set is exactly the D6 note's exclusions. Holds in the declared-object case.
- **Should-fix 2 — stack.zod.ts:4520 and :4539.** `fieldsByObject` merges `objectExtensions` by `extend`, so an object this stack knows ONLY through an extension (someone else's object, which is what an extension is for) counts as resolved and is judged against the extension's fields alone. A child following `sales_order.currency_code` where `currency_code` is the owner's field and this stack only extends `sales_order` is refused "'sales_order' declares no field 'currency_code'" — a contract-valid stack refused at `defineStack`. The precedent at :4419 shares the stance, and claim amend 1 ordered parity, but parity with a false refusal is still a false refusal of what ruling A admits. Remedy: keep the names declared in `config.objects` apart from those reached only via `extend`, and skip (a) and (b) when the parent is extension-only (an unresolved parent is not a wrong one, the precedent's own words). The precedent's identical gap is the seat's follow-up, not this card's.
- **Nit N1 — stack.zod.ts:4590.** When the summary declares `fixed` or `dynamic` currency, the message says it "would show as a bare number"; a `fixed` one shows in its fixed code. The refusal itself is right (the roll-up is in the parent's currency); only the sentence is off.
- **Nit N2 — stack.zod.ts:4576-4577.** With `relationshipField` omitted and two back relations, (b) skips, while the engine (`engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts`, the scan at the `fkField` resolution) takes the first `master_detail`/`lookup` to the parent in declaration order. A roll-up the engine will run through the followed `master_detail` can go undeclared here. Documented in the JSDoc; a follow-up or an accepted deviation, since the registry (#31911) is the other reader.

**packages/spec/liveness/field.json** (implementing: the ledger the describe texts' PLANNED state rests on) — see ③ deviation 3. Accepted.

**Prose-face nits (fixable without moving the reviewed code):**
- **Nit N3 — PR body `Skills-docs:` line; .changeset line 9.** SKILL.md's grammar is `follow-up owed — FILES | follow-up #N`, and the seat rewrites `owed — FILES` to `#N`; every changeset precedent spells `Skills-docs: follow-up #N`. The body's `follow-up owed #31957` matches neither form, and the changeset still carries `owed — FILES` without the card number. Spell both `Skills-docs: follow-up #31957 — skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md`.
- **Nit N4 — PR body (Liveness paragraph).** `scripts/liveness/undrilled-containers.baseline.json` does not exist; the file is `packages/spec/scripts/liveness/undrilled-containers.baseline.json`. The ledger note names the file without a path and is fine.

**Tried and did not break:** a three-level chain (refused at two segments, with the "give the parent its own code field" remedy); a self-referencing `master_detail` (passes the object door, judged by the stack door against the same map); two paths through two `master_detail` fields sharing a rate field (refused: two parent rows); a summary over a path-following `formula` ((b) applies, since `recordCurrencyPathOf` reads the config, not the type); a `count` over following children (skipped); an own-code child under an undeclared summary (skipped, D6's first bullet stays the registry's); a path whose segment 2 is itself a `record`-mode currency (refused at (a): not a code field).

Summary: 0 must-fix, 2 should-fix (delta review of their fixes owed to this reviewer), 4 nits.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-kwlb0r`
Reviewed-by: `fable-subagent of session_01QsR2jUe9c6YdtNkrzUnMUd`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5553a6fd37a166b1baec6201d43c259c060b4f94`
Local-runs: none
